purpose: The distinct facts behind WP1's 76 decisive conditions, phrased as questions a non-lawyer can answer. No question asks the user to pick an Annex category.
status: DRAFT - unreviewed. Each question carries its source condition so a reviewer can check question -> condition -> official text in one pass.

evidence_expectation_legend.MANUFACTURER_ONLY: requires knowledge the manufacturer holds; not evidenced from public documents

facts.question: What exactly is placed on the market as one product? List what is sold together, and what is sold separately.
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 3(1): components placed on the market separately are products in their own right. Everything downstream depends on this.

worked_example.yes: A sensor and its hub sold as one boxed kit = one product. The same hub also sold alone = a second product.
worked_example.no: Listing everything your company makes, rather than the one item being assessed.

facts.question: Is the product made available on the EU market?

worked_example.yes: Sold through an EU distributor, or shipped to EU customers from outside.
worked_example.no: Built and used only at your own sites, never supplied to anyone.

facts.superseded_why: a yes/no cannot express planned sale (SCP-09), trade-fair display (SCP-08) or own use (OWN-01)

facts.question: Is it supplied in the course of a commercial activity, whether paid or free of charge?

worked_example.yes: Supplied free of charge but as part of a paid support offering.
worked_example.no: A hobby project published with no commercial activity around it.

facts.user_why: The CRA only covers products supplied as part of a business activity. Giving something away for free can still count: what matters is whether you earn from it in some way, for example by charging for support, for a platform around it, or by requiring users' personal data. Truly non-commercial projects, such as most volunteer open-source work, are outside.

legal_basis.quote: in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge

Supply in the course of a commercial activity might be characterised not only by charging a price for a product with digital elements, but also by charging a price for technical support services where this does not serve only the recuperation of actual costs, by an intention to monetise

facts.question: Can the product exchange data with another device or network — directly or indirectly, by wire, radio, or a physical interface such as USB?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1) with Art. 3(8)(9)(10). Not limited to internet connection.

worked_example.yes: A meter that sends readings over radio to a collector; a device that syncs over USB.
worked_example.no: A mechanical timer with no electronic interface of any kind.

facts.superseded_why: capability and intended purpose are different tests; Art. 2(1) asks about intended or foreseeable use

facts.question: If no connection is intended, could one reasonably be foreseen in use?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1) 'reasonably foreseeable use'

worked_example.yes: A service port you document for installers, even if end users never use it.
worked_example.no: A sealed unit with no port and no radio.

facts.user_why: Even if you do not intend a connection, the CRA applies if users can reasonably be expected to connect the product anyway, for example through a port you have not disabled.

legal_basis.quote: the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use of which includes

facts.question: Is the product covered by any of these? MDR 2017/745 · IVDR 2017/746 · Reg. 2019/2144 (vehicles) · certified under Reg. 2018/1139 (aviation) · Dir. 2014/90/EU (marine) · Reg. (EU) No 168/2013 (two- and three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles) · a same-specification spare part · developed exclusively for defence or to process classified information
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(2)-(7), plus Art. 2(5) delegated acts. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1535 excludes products within Reg. (EU) No 168/2013 - BUT NOT L1e category vehicles designed to pedal, which remain in CRA scope. Each limb is a separate question in the full assessment.

worked_example.yes: A moped or quadricycle within Reg. (EU) No 168/2013 — excluded by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1535.
worked_example.no: A speed pedelec or other L1e vehicle designed to pedal — expressly carved back IN by that same Regulation.

facts.delegated_act_rule: Check whether an APPLICABLE delegated act covers this product, never whether any delegated act exists. As at 12 October 2026 the only one found under Art. 2(5) is Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1535. Re-check each release.
facts.superseded_by: EXCLUSION_SCREEN + one follow-up per ticked exclusion
facts.superseded_why: each exclusion has its own condition (certified, exclusively, identical spec, designed to pedal)

facts.question: Are you the manufacturer, importer, distributor, integrator, or open-source steward?

worked_example.yes: You design it, have it built, and sell it under your own brand - manufacturer.
worked_example.no: You resell it unchanged in its original packaging - distributor.

facts.question: When was this product first made available on the EU market?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 3(21), decisive for Art. 69(2)

worked_example.yes: The date the first unit was supplied to a customer or distributor in the EU.
worked_example.no: The date development finished, or the date of the press release.

facts.superseded_why: The CRA applies to individual units, not product types (Blue Guide 2.2, TYPE-02). A type's first launch date protects no later unit.

facts.question: Has the product changed since it was placed on the market?

worked_example.yes: A firmware release that adds a feature after units shipped.
worked_example.no: A change made before any unit was supplied.

facts.question: Does the change affect how secure the product is — for example how it authenticates users, protects stored or transmitted data, or delivers updates?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 3(30) limb (a): a change affecting compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Annex I, Part I. The MVP cannot decide this, so it must be asked, and UNKNOWN must never be read as NO.

worked_example.yes: A change that alters how the product authenticates users or handles updates.
worked_example.no: A change to an icon or a translation string.

facts.user_why: A change that affects whether the product still meets the CRA's security requirements is also a substantial modification. That needs a security assessment, which this tool cannot do, so a change of this kind is flagged for review.

legal_basis.quote: which affects the compliance of the product with digital elements with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I

facts.question: Does that change modify the intended purpose for which the product was assessed?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 3(30) limb (b)

worked_example.yes: Adding remote unlocking to a device previously sold as a monitor.
worked_example.no: A performance optimisation with no new function.

facts.user_why: A change that alters what the product is meant to be used for is a substantial modification, and brings the product under the CRA's main requirements.

legal_basis.quote: which results in a modification to the intended purpose for which the product with digital elements has been assessed

facts.question: In one sentence, what is this product for? What would a buyer say it does?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 7(1)/8(1): core functionality determines the category. B2 recital 2.

worked_example.yes: 'It detects whether a trap has caught a rodent and tells the pest controller.'
worked_example.no: 'It uses Linux, a camera and TLS.' - that is components, not purpose.

facts.user_why: The class depends on what the product is for, not on every function it contains. A smartphone contains an operating system, but it is not an operating system. Describe your product as a buyer would; the following questions test what that means.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements which have the core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III shall be considered to be important products

The integration of a product with digital elements which has the core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III shall not in itself render the product in which it is integrated subject to

facts.question: Does the product merely contain a component that performs one of these functions, or is that function what the product is for?
facts.why_we_ask: B2 recital 4 and B7 section 3.4: a smartphone is not an operating system; a router with a firewall is still a router.

worked_example.yes: A router that contains a firewall is still a router.
worked_example.no: Calling a smartphone an operating system because it runs one.

facts.question: Does the product provide any security-related functionality, such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage, random number generation or a trusted execution environment?
facts.why_we_ask: Shared condition of III-I-13/14/15

certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Evidence that security functionality exists and was evaluated. Absence proves nothing.

worked_example.yes: Secure boot, key storage, a trusted execution environment.
worked_example.no: A password field in an app.

facts.user_why: Chips are only in these categories if they provide security functions such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage or random number generation.

legal_basis.quote: They additionally provide security-related functionalities, such as encryption, authentication, secure key storage, random number generation

facts.question: Does that security functionality aim to secure OTHER products, networks or services — beyond the chip itself?
facts.why_we_ask: The decisive limiter in III-I-13/14/15. A chip protecting only its own operation is outside.

worked_example.yes: A chip that anchors the secure boot chain of the whole device.
worked_example.no: A chip whose crypto only verifies its own firmware image.

facts.user_why: A chip only counts if its security functions protect other products, networks or services, such as a secure boot chain for the device it sits in. Protecting only its own internal operation does not count.

legal_basis.quote: that aim to secure other products, networks or services beyond the microcontroller itself

facts.question: Is the product an integrated circuit — a microprocessor, microcontroller, ASIC or FPGA?

worked_example.yes: A microcontroller sold to device makers.
worked_example.no: A finished appliance that contains one.

facts.superseded_why: categories depend on which kind of IC

facts.question: Does it provide tamper evidence, tamper resistance or tamper response?

certification_proxy.marker: FIPS 140-2/140-3 physical security level; PCI PTS HSM listing
certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Holding the certificate is strong evidence the condition is met. NOT holding it proves nothing - certification is not required for the category to apply. Inferring exclusion from absence would be a false negative of the AC-02 kind.

worked_example.yes: An enclosure that zeroises keys when opened; an active shield.
worked_example.no: A warranty-void sticker.

facts.user_why: Tamper evidence, resistance or response against physical attack moves a chip into a higher class, and is required for secure elements.

legal_basis.quote: including tamper evidence, resistance or response
Secure elements are microcontrollers or microprocessors with security-related functionalities, including tamper evidence, resistance or response

facts.question: What AVA_VAN level is it designed to provide, under the Common Criteria?
facts.why_we_ask: III-II-03/04 require level 2 or 3 exactly; IV-03 requires AT LEAST AVA_VAN.4. Level 1 matters: it fails both (WP5 MP-24..26).

certification_proxy.marker: Common Criteria certificate stating EAL augmented with AVA_VAN.n (Common Criteria Portal, BSI, ANSSI)
certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Holding the certificate is strong evidence the condition is met. NOT holding it proves nothing - certification is not required for the category to apply. Inferring exclusion from absence would be a false negative of the AC-02 kind.
certification_proxy.scheme_note: Record the issuing scheme as well as the level. Newer evaluations rest on exact protection-profile conformance rather than an EAL number, and mutual recognition under the CCRA is capped below the levels these conditions cite, so a level 4 or 5 claim may rest on a national scheme.

worked_example.yes: 'EAL4+ augmented with AVA_VAN.5' on the certificate. Record the issuing scheme too.
worked_example.no: A vendor claim of being 'highly secure' with no certificate.

facts.user_why: AVA_VAN is the Common Criteria rating for resistance to attack. Level 2 or 3 makes a tamper-resistant chip Class II; level 4 or higher makes it a secure element, which is critical. A certificate is good evidence; not having one proves nothing.

legal_basis.quote: designed to provide protection of AVA_VAN level 2 or 3
Secure elements are designed to provide protection of at least AVA_VAN.4

facts.question: Does it communicate on the public Internet, directly or via other equipment?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-16, III-I-18

worked_example.yes: Reaches a cloud service directly or through a hub.
worked_example.no: Talks only to a paired handset over Bluetooth, with no internet path.

facts.user_why: Some categories cover only products that communicate on the public internet, directly or through another device such as a phone or a hub.

legal_basis.quote: communicate on the public Internet, whether directly or via other equipment

facts.question: Is it intended for use in a home, as opposed to an office, industrial or public setting?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-16, III-I-17

worked_example.yes: Sold for homes, through consumer retail.
worked_example.no: Sold for office buildings. If both - say both; that is a real answer.

facts.user_why: The smart home categories cover products for people's homes. The same device sold for offices, shops or hotels falls outside them, though the CRA itself still applies.

legal_basis.quote: in a residential setting

facts.question: Can it be controlled or managed remotely from another system?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-17

worked_example.yes: Controlled from an app while the user is away.
worked_example.no: Operated only by a button on the device.

facts.superseded_why: boolean could not carry the open proximity case

facts.question: Is the product's purpose to protect the physical security of people in that setting?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-17. Monitoring pests, energy or comfort is not physical security of consumers.

worked_example.yes: A lock, an alarm, an intruder camera.
worked_example.no: A device that monitors energy use, comfort or pests.

facts.user_why: Smart home security products are a listed category. What counts is whether the product's purpose is protecting people's physical security, for example against intruders. Watching pests, energy use or comfort does not count, even with a camera.

legal_basis.quote: protect the physical security of consumers in a residential setting

facts.question: Does it centrally control products that protect physical security, such as locks or alarms?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-17, fourth limb

worked_example.yes: A hub or app that manages locks and alarms together.
worked_example.no: A hub that only manages lighting and heating.

facts.user_why: A hub or app that controls locks, alarms or security cameras in the home is in the same category as those products, even if it protects nothing itself.

legal_basis.quote: as well as hardware and software that centrally control such products

facts.question: Is securely storing, processing or managing sensitive data, or performing cryptographic operations, what the product is FOR?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-01, IV-03, and the IV-02 exclusion gate

worked_example.yes: A hardware security module; a secure element.
worked_example.no: A product that uses TLS like almost every connected product.

facts.user_why: Hardware security devices are critical products. The first condition: is protecting sensitive data or performing cryptographic operations what the device is for?

legal_basis.quote: securely store, process, or manage sensitive data or perform cryptographic operations

facts.question: Does it consist of multiple discrete components inside a hardware envelope that resists physical attack?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-01

certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Holding the certificate is strong evidence the condition is met. NOT holding it proves nothing - certification is not required for the category to apply. Inferring exclusion from absence would be a false negative of the AC-02 kind.

worked_example.yes: A payment terminal with a tamper-responsive enclosure.
worked_example.no: A single chip with no multi-component enclosure.

facts.question: Does it provide the means to control other devices?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02, III-I-16

worked_example.yes: Issues commands that change another device's state.
worked_example.no: Only reads from other devices.

facts.user_why: A smart meter gateway lets the metering system control other devices. A device that only measures and reports controls nothing.

legal_basis.quote: provide the means to control other devices

facts.question: Does it control communication between metering components and authorised third parties such as utilities?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02 gateway limb

certification_proxy.marker: Certification under protection profile BSI-CC-PP-0073 and conformity with BSI TR-03109
certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Holding the certificate is strong evidence the condition is met. NOT holding it proves nothing - certification is not required for the category to apply. Inferring exclusion from absence would be a false negative of the AC-02 kind.

worked_example.yes: Mediates between meters and the utility's systems.
worked_example.no: A meter that simply transmits its own readings.

facts.user_why: Smart meter gateways are critical products. A gateway controls the communication between the metering system and outside parties such as the utility. A meter that only sends its own readings is not a gateway.

legal_basis.quote: control communication between components in or connected to smart metering systems

facts.question: Which commodity is metered?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02: B2 names electricity, extended to gas and heat. Water is not named.

worked_example.yes: Electricity, gas, heat - named in the technical description.
worked_example.no: Water, which is not named; this is a known open question.

facts.superseded_why: water is not an energy carrier; name misled

facts.question: Does it authenticate or authorise people, devices or systems, or control their access to digital resources or physical locations?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-01

worked_example.yes: Single sign-on; a badge reader controlling a door.
worked_example.no: An app with a login screen that calls someone else's identity service.

facts.user_why: Identity and access management products are a listed category: products that check who someone is, or decide what they may access, including physical access readers.

legal_basis.quote: provide mechanisms for authentication or authorisation
control access of natural persons, legal persons, devices or systems to digital resources or physical locations

facts.question: Does it let users access, display and interact with web content and services hosted on servers?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-02. A browser engine, web protocols and script execution are what browsers 'typically include', not conditions (WP5 MP-01).

worked_example.yes: An embedded web view loading remote pages, even with scripts disabled.
worked_example.no: A help screen rendering local static HTML only.

facts.previous_question: Does it access, render and interact with web content over web protocols, with a browser engine and script execution?
facts.user_why: Browsers are a listed category, including browser components built into other apps. What matters is letting users open and use web content from servers; it does not need every feature of a full browser.

legal_basis.quote: enable end users to access, render, and interact with web content and services hosted on servers

facts.question: Does it store passwords, and generate, share or integrate them with other applications?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-03

worked_example.yes: A vault that generates, stores and fills credentials.
worked_example.no: An app that remembers one login for itself.

facts.superseded_why: bundled illustrative activities as conditions (WP5 finding 1)

facts.question: Does it detect, search for, remove or quarantine malicious software?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-04

worked_example.yes: Scans for and quarantines malicious code.
worked_example.no: Reports that a file changed, without judging whether it is malicious.

facts.user_why: Antivirus and anti-malware software is a listed category: software that finds malicious code, or removes or quarantines it.

legal_basis.quote: detect or search for malicious software or code on devices, or remove or quarantine such software or code

facts.question: Does it establish an encrypted logical tunnel built from the resources of a physical or virtual network?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-05. Using TLS for its own traffic is not this.

worked_example.yes: A client or gateway establishing an encrypted tunnel.
worked_example.no: An app that uses TLS for its own traffic.

facts.user_why: VPN products are a listed category: products that set up an encrypted tunnel over a network. An app that only encrypts its own traffic is not a VPN.

legal_basis.quote: establish an encrypted logical tunnel that is constructed from the system resources of a physical or virtual network

facts.question: Does it monitor connected network elements AND control their network operations and configuration?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-06

worked_example.yes: Pushes configuration to switches and routers.
worked_example.no: Displays network status without changing anything.

facts.superseded_why: AND-bundle; inclusion list overrides monitoring (WP5 finding 2)

facts.question: Does it collect data from multiple sources, correlate it, and present it as actionable security information?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-07. SOAR is generally not SIEM (B7 section 3.4).

worked_example.yes: Collects logs from many sources and correlates them into alerts.
worked_example.no: Stores logs for later search without correlation.

facts.question: Does it manage system startup after power-on or restart: initialising hardware and loading or handing control to the operating system?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-08. Selecting boot options is part of the description, but single-stage boot loaders are expressly included, so it is not required (WP5 MP-07).

worked_example.yes: UEFI firmware; a single-stage boot loader that loads one fixed kernel.
worked_example.no: An updater that replaces a kernel file.

facts.previous_question: Does it manage system startup — initialising hardware, loading the OS, selecting boot options?
facts.user_why: Boot managers are a listed category: firmware or software that starts a system after power-on and hands over to the operating system. Single-stage boot loaders count too.

legal_basis.quote: manage the process of initial system startup after power on/restart
single-stage and multi-stage boot loaders

facts.question: Does it manage the lifecycle of digital certificates or their associated keys?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-09. Merely validating certificates is not this.

worked_example.yes: Issues, renews and revokes certificates.
worked_example.no: Validates certificates using the OS trust store.

facts.user_why: Certificate issuance and PKI software is a listed category: software that creates, issues, renews or revokes digital certificates, or manages the keys that belong to them. A key store with no certificates does not count.

legal_basis.quote: manage the validation, creation, issuance, distribution, status publication, renewal or revocation of digital certificates

facts.question: Does it connect a device to a network through an interface driver API — a network card, adapter or virtual interface?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-10

worked_example.yes: A network card or adapter with its driver interface.
worked_example.no: A USB storage controller.

facts.user_why: Network interfaces are a listed category: network cards and adapters, and virtual network interfaces sold as products.

legal_basis.quote: This category includes but is not limited to wired and wireless network interface cards, controllers and adapters

facts.question: Does it abstract the hardware and control the execution of other software?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-11

worked_example.yes: An RTOS sold to device makers.
worked_example.no: A phone that runs one.

certification_proxy.marker: NIAP General Purpose Operating System Protection Profile; BSI Operating System Protection Profile (OSPP)
certification_proxy.use: POSITIVE ONLY. Evidence the product was evaluated as an operating system. Absence proves nothing.

facts.user_why: Operating systems are a listed category: software that sits between the hardware and other software and controls how that software runs.

legal_basis.quote: provide an abstract interface of the underlying hardware and control the execution of software

facts.question: Does it route traffic between networks, modulate signals for IP communication, or forward packets with a management plane?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-12

worked_example.yes: A router, managed switch, modem or access point.
worked_example.no: A device that merely connects as a client.

facts.question: Does it process natural-language requests and act on them by reaching services or controlling devices?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-16

worked_example.yes: Understands spoken requests and acts on them.
worked_example.no: Responds to a few fixed voice commands offline.

facts.user_why: Smart home virtual assistants are a listed category: products that take spoken or written requests and act on them, by reaching services or controlling devices in the home.

legal_basis.quote: process demands, tasks or questions based on natural language prompts

facts.question: Is it designed or intended for play by children under 14? Some products are not treated as toys even when children use them — for example playground equipment for public use, toy steam engines, and slings and catapults.
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-18 via Directive 2009/48/EC Art. 2, including its Annex I list of products not considered toys. From 01.08.2030 the reference resolves to Reg. (EU) 2025/2509 by its Art. 56 correlation clause.

worked_example.yes: Designed for play by children under 14.
worked_example.no: A hobby kit marketed to adults.

facts.user_why: Connected toys are a listed category, but only products that count as toys under EU toy safety law: designed or intended for play by children under 14.

legal_basis.quote: that are covered by Directive 2009/48/EC

facts.question: Does it have social interactive features such as speaking or filming, or location tracking? Proximity detection alone does not count.
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-18, including its express negative condition

worked_example.yes: A microphone and speaker for two-way interaction; location reporting.
worked_example.no: Proximity detection only - expressly not location tracking.

facts.user_why: A connected toy is in the category if it can talk, listen or film, or if it tracks where the child is. Only noticing that someone is nearby does not count as tracking.

legal_basis.quote: that have embedded technologies that enable inbound and outbound communication, such as keyboard, microphone, speaker or camera
the toy is not to be considered to have location tracking features

facts.question: Is it worn on the body, directly or via clothing or accessories?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-19

worked_example.yes: A wristband, smartwatch or smart garment.
worked_example.no: A device clipped to a bag but not worn on the body.

facts.user_why: Wearables are a listed category when they monitor health or are made for children. First: is it worn on the body, directly or through clothing or accessories?

legal_basis.quote: worn on the body directly or via clothing or accessories

facts.question: Does it regularly or continuously sense and process information relevant to the user's health?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-19

worked_example.yes: Continuous heart-rate or activity sensing.
worked_example.no: A watch that only tells the time.

facts.user_why: A wearable is in the category if it regularly or continuously senses information about the wearer's health, such as heart rate or other body measurements.

legal_basis.quote: regularly or continuously, sense and further process information, including body metrics, relevant to the user's health

facts.question: Is it intended for use by and for individuals under 14?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-19, second limb

worked_example.yes: A child safety wearable.
worked_example.no: An adult fitness tracker.

facts.user_why: Wearables made for children under 14 are in the category even without any health monitoring, for example child safety watches.

legal_basis.quote: Personal wearable products that are intended for the use by and for children
This category includes but is not limited to child safety wearables.

facts.question: Does it execute, manage or orchestrate virtual machines, or manage the lifecycle of containers?
facts.why_we_ask: III-II-01

worked_example.yes: A type 1 hypervisor; a container runtime.
worked_example.no: A sandbox isolating a single process.

facts.superseded_why: boolean could not carry the open orchestrator case

facts.question: Does it monitor and restrict network traffic, or detect or respond to intrusions?
facts.why_we_ask: III-II-02. No industrial-use condition exists.

worked_example.yes: A firewall or IPS, consumer or industrial - no industrial condition applies.
worked_example.no: A router that happens to include firewall features.

facts.user_why: Firewalls and intrusion detection or prevention systems are Class II, whether for homes or industry. A router that also has a firewall stays a router; tick this only if filtering or detecting intrusions is what the product is for.

legal_basis.quote: protect a connected network or system from unauthorized access by monitoring and restricting data communication traffic
monitor traffic once it has entered the network environment for suspicious activity

facts.question: Is it a secure element — a chip that stores or manages credentials — or a card containing one?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-03

worked_example.yes: A TPM, eUICC or payment card chip.
worked_example.no: A general microcontroller with a crypto library.

facts.superseded_why: question built in the descriptive 'typically stores ... credentials'; IV-03 is decided by the four facts it is derived from

facts.question: Do the radio equipment cybersecurity rules (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30) cover the product?
facts.why_we_ask: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 Art. 1, applying RED Art. 3(3)(d), (e) and (f). Its Art. 2 derogates: MDR/IVDR products are out entirely; products under Reg. 2018/1139, Reg. 2019/2144 or Dir. 2019/520 are out of limbs (e) and (f). Not a CRA scope question - radio equipment is fully in CRA scope - but these requirements have applied since 1 August 2025, so a CRA-only timeline answer would be falsely reassuring.

worked_example.yes: An internet-connected device with a Wi-Fi or cellular radio, placed on the market after 1 August 2025.
worked_example.no: A wired-only product with no radio, or radio equipment outside the Delegated Regulation's listed categories.

facts.output_rule: POINTER ONLY. The tool must not assess RED conformity - v4 section 2.3 keeps this out of scope. It states that other requirements may already apply and that the user should check them separately. Harmonised standards for the RED Delegated Regulation are the EN 18031 series, cited in the OJ; they are NOT CRA standards.
facts.user_why: Before the CRA applies, radio products may already have cybersecurity rules under the radio equipment rules: since 1 August 2025, for internet-connected radio equipment, equipment handling personal data, and equipment that can transfer money.

legal_basis.quote: radio equipment that can communicate itself over the internet

facts.revision_note: 13 Oct 2026: no longer asked as one compound question. Derived from four atomic facts: covered if radio AND (internet-connected OR (toy, childcare or worn on the body AND can process personal, traffic or location data)). Art. 1(3) (money transfer) needs internet connection, so it adds no case. Art. 2 derogations (MDR/IVDR; Reg. 2018/1139, 2019/2144, Dir. 2019/520 for limbs (e),(f)) are outside CRA scope already, except electronic road toll systems, which this tool does not ask about.

facts.question: Is storing passwords, on the device or on a server, what this product is for?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-03: 'store passwords, locally on a device or on a remote server'. Generation, sharing and filling are listed as examples, not conditions (WP5 MP-02).

worked_example.yes: A password vault, even one with no generator.
worked_example.no: A notes app that happens to have one encrypted field: storing passwords is not its purpose.

facts.question_hint: Generating, sharing or auto-filling passwords is typical but not required.
facts.user_why: Password managers are a listed category. What counts is whether storing passwords is the product's purpose, not whether it has a password field.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements that store passwords, locally on a device or on a remote server

facts.question: Does it monitor connected network elements such as servers, routers, switches or printers?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-06: 'by monitoring them'. Not decisive on its own: the description also includes dedicated configuration management systems (WP5 MP-04).

worked_example.yes: Polls switches and shows their status and alarms.
worked_example.no: Shows only its own status.

facts.question: Does it control the network operations or configuration of other network elements?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-06: 'controlling their network operations and configuration'.

worked_example.yes: Pushes configuration to routers and switches; an SDN controller.
worked_example.no: Displays network status without changing anything.

facts.user_why: Network management systems are a listed category. What decides is whether the product controls how other network equipment operates or is configured. A dashboard that only shows status does not.

legal_basis.quote: controlling their network operations and configuration

facts.question: How can the product be controlled or managed from another system?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-17: 'can be controlled or managed remotely from other systems'. Control from a nearby phone only is an open question (WP5 MP-14).

worked_example.yes: From an app over the internet or a home hub: NETWORK_REMOTE.
worked_example.no: Only by buttons on the device: NONE.

facts.user_why: Smart home security products are covered when another system can control or manage them, such as an app over the internet or a home hub. Control only from a phone standing next to the device is a case the law does not clearly settle.

legal_basis.quote: can be controlled or managed remotely from other systems

facts.question: Is the product itself an integrated circuit? If so, which kind?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-13 (microprocessor: external memory), III-I-14 (microcontroller: integrated memory), III-I-15 (ASIC/FPGA), III-II-03/04, IV-03 (microcontroller or microprocessor).

worked_example.yes: A microcontroller sold to device makers: MICROCONTROLLER.
worked_example.no: A finished appliance that contains one: NOT_AN_IC.

condition_values.SOC_UNCLEAR: Matches III-I-13 or III-I-14; both are Class I, so the class is unaffected (WP5 MP-12). IV-03 accepts either.

facts.user_why: Several categories cover chips: microprocessors, microcontrollers and custom chips with security functions, and secure elements. If your product is not itself a chip, all of them are ruled out with one answer.

legal_basis.quote: integrated circuits that carry out central processing functions integrating memory
integrated circuits that carry out central processing functions relying on external memory and peripherals

facts.question: Which commodity does the metering system measure?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02 gateway limb: electricity is named, and gas or heat as 'other sources of energy'. Water is not an energy source (WP1; A4-02).

worked_example.yes: Electricity, gas or heat.
worked_example.no: Water: the gateway limb does not match, and the second limb is an open question.

facts.user_why: The gateway category names electricity, and gas or heat as other sources of energy. Water is not a source of energy, so a water gateway falls outside that part of the category.

legal_basis.quote: smart meter gateways related to smart metering systems measuring electricity
measuring consumption of other sources of energy such as gas or heat

facts.question: Does it collect data from multiple sources?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-07, first of three required conditions (WP5 MP-06).

worked_example.yes: Logs from firewalls, servers and endpoints.
worked_example.no: The logs of one firewall only.

facts.user_why: Security event management (SIEM) systems are a listed category. They gather data from many sources; a tool reading one device's logs is not one.

legal_basis.quote: collect data from multiple sources

facts.question: Does it analyse and correlate that data?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-07, second required condition.

worked_example.yes: Correlates events across sources into incidents.
worked_example.no: Stores logs for later search without correlation.

facts.user_why: A SIEM analyses and correlates the data it gathers, rather than only storing it.

legal_basis.quote: analyse and correlate that data

facts.question: Is the result presented as actionable information for security purposes, such as threat detection, forensics or compliance?
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-07, third required condition. SOAR is generally not SIEM (B7 section 3.4).

worked_example.yes: Security alerts and incident timelines.
worked_example.no: Application performance dashboards (WP5 MP-05).

facts.user_why: A SIEM turns that data into information for security, such as detecting threats or incidents. Correlating data for performance or business reporting does not count.

legal_basis.quote: present it as actionable information for security-related purposes, such as threat and incident detection, forensic analysis or compliance purposes

facts.question: Which of these does the product do? Select all that apply.
facts.why_we_ask: III-I-12 has three limbs, each with its own qualifier: routers; modems intended for connection to the Internet; switches with a management plane (WP5 MP-10, MP-11).

worked_example.yes: A home router with built-in modem: ROUTER and INTERNET_MODEM.
worked_example.no: A device that only connects as a Wi-Fi client: NONE.

facts.user_why: Routers, internet modems and managed switches are a listed category. Each has its own condition: a modem only counts if it is for internet connection, and a switch only if it has a management plane.

legal_basis.quote: Modems intended for the connection to the Internet are hardware products
that have a management plane

facts.question: Does it run virtual machines or containers? Which describes it best?
facts.why_we_ask: III-II-01: hypervisors, and container runtimes on a single host that allocate resources and manage containers. Multi-host orchestrators are an open question (WP5 MP-21).

worked_example.yes: A type 1 hypervisor; a container runtime.
worked_example.no: A sandbox isolating one process.

facts.user_why: Hypervisors and container runtimes are Class II products. A tool that only schedules containers across machines, without running them itself, is a case the law does not clearly settle.

legal_basis.quote: enable the execution, management and orchestration of virtual machines
manage the execution and lifecycle of containers running on a single host operating system

facts.question: Is it built from multiple discrete components, rather than a single chip?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-01: 'consist of multiple discrete components'.

worked_example.yes: A payment terminal or HSM board.
worked_example.no: A single secure chip.

facts.user_why: The critical category covers devices built from several components, such as a payment terminal or a hardware security module. A single chip falls under other categories.

legal_basis.quote: consist of multiple discrete components

facts.question: Do those components sit inside a hardware enclosure that gives tamper evidence, resistance or response against physical attack?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-01: 'incorporating a hardware physical envelope providing tamper evidence, resistance or response' (WP5 MP-27).

worked_example.yes: A tamper-responsive HSM enclosure that erases keys when opened.
worked_example.no: An ordinary industrial PC case.

facts.user_why: What makes these devices critical is a physical enclosure that shows, resists or reacts to tampering, for example by erasing keys when it is opened. An ordinary case does not count.

legal_basis.quote: incorporating a hardware physical envelope providing tamper evidence, resistance or response as countermeasures against physical attacks

facts.question: Is the product's core functionality an advanced security purpose, such as secure cryptoprocessing, as opposed to a feature it also has?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02 second limb: 'other devices for advanced security purposes, including for secure cryptoprocessing'. It has no technical description, so a TRUE answer leads to expert review, never to a match (WP1 open question).

worked_example.yes: A device whose core function is cryptoprocessing for other systems.
worked_example.no: A water meter that encrypts its own readings.

facts.user_why: The critical category also mentions other devices for advanced security purposes, such as secure cryptoprocessing, but the EU has not described them further. If your product's purpose is of that kind, the tool will flag it for expert review instead of deciding.

legal_basis.quote: other devices for advanced security purposes, including for secure cryptoprocessing

facts.question: Is the product a high-risk AI system under the AI Act, and on which basis?
facts.why_we_ask: CRA Art. 12 sets the conformity route for high-risk AI. The AI Act as amended by Reg. 2026/1744 treats the bases differently: Annex III from 2.12.2027; Annex I Section A from 2.8.2028; Annex I Section B (e.g. machinery) outside Art. 43 (cases AI-01, AI-05, AI-06).

worked_example.yes: An AI safety component in a product under Annex I Section A legislation.
worked_example.no: No AI system, or one that is not high-risk: NONE.

facts.user_why: If your product is also a high-risk AI system, the AI Act can change which conformity procedure you use. The dates differ by basis, and for machinery the AI Act was changed in 2026 in a way the CRA does not yet reflect.

legal_basis.quote: the relevant conformity assessment procedure provided for in Article 43

legal_basis.cite: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 2(2) and Art. 113(c), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
legal_basis.ref: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Art. 2(2) and Art. 113(c), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

facts.question: Is the product classified as an electronic health record (EHR) system under Regulation (EU) 2025/327?
facts.why_we_ask: CRA Art. 32(5a), inserted by the EHDS: EHR systems follow the EHDS conformity procedure from 26.3.2027 (EHR-01).

worked_example.yes: An EHR system placed on the market for healthcare providers.
worked_example.no: A fitness app that stores the user's own workouts.

facts.user_why: Electronic health record systems follow the conformity procedure of the European Health Data Space rules instead of the CRA's own procedure, from 26 March 2027.

facts.question: When are, or were, the units you are assessing placed on the market? Each unit counts on its own.
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 69(2) and 71(2): units placed before 11.12.2027 are exempt from the main requirements unless substantially modified; units placed later must comply, however long the type has been sold (TYPE-01/02). RED DA: units placed from 1.8.2025.

worked_example.yes: Units shipped from January 2028 on: 2028-01 onward.
worked_example.no: 'We launched this model in 2024' - that is the type's launch, not the units' placing date.

facts.question_hint: If you are asking about both stock already shipped and future production, assess them separately.
facts.user_why: The CRA's main requirements apply to units placed on the market from 11 December 2027. Units placed earlier are exempt unless they are substantially changed later. This is about the units you are asking about, not when the model was launched: later units of an older model must comply.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements that have been placed on the market before 11 December 2027 shall be subject to the requirements set out in this Regulation only if, from that date, those products are subject to a substantial modification
This Regulation shall apply from 11 December 2027

facts.question: When was the change made, or when will it be?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 69(2): only substantial modifications made from 11.12.2027 bring earlier units under the main requirements (LIFE-10).

worked_example.yes: Firmware 3.0 rolled out to installed units in March 2028.
worked_example.no: No change since placing: leave empty.

facts.user_why: Only changes made from 11 December 2027 can bring earlier units under the main requirements.

legal_basis.quote: only if, from that date, those products are subject to a substantial modification

facts.question: Does the product hold an EU type-examination certificate or approval decision covering cybersecurity under other EU harmonisation legislation?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 69(1): such certificates stay valid until 11.6.2028, or their earlier expiry, unless that legislation provides otherwise (LIFE-07, LIFE-11).

worked_example.yes: A certificate under other harmonisation legislation covering cybersecurity requirements, expiring 2029.
worked_example.no: A test report or a self-declaration: not a certificate.

facts.user_why: If your product already holds an EU type-examination certificate covering cybersecurity under other EU product rules, that certificate stays valid for a while under the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: shall remain valid until 11 June 2028, unless they expire before that date

facts.question: Is what you place on the market hardware, software, or an online service?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 3(1), 3(2): products with digital elements are hardware or software, including remote data processing the product needs. A standalone online service is not (BND-03, BND-04).

worked_example.yes: A device with its companion cloud backend: HARDWARE plus REMOTE_DATA_PROCESSING.
worked_example.no: A web application with no product of yours behind it: SAAS_ONLY.

facts.user_why: The CRA covers products: hardware and software, including a cloud backend that your product needs in order to work. A purely online service with no product behind it is not covered.

legal_basis.quote: ‘product with digital elements’ means a software or hardware product and its remote data processing solutions
the absence of which would prevent the product with digital elements from performing one of its functions

facts.question: Where is the product in its life on the EU market?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1), 3(22): the CRA applies to products made available on the EU market. Planned sale is assessed prospectively (SCP-09); display at a trade fair (SCP-08) and own use (OWN-01) are not making available.

worked_example.yes: On sale in the EU, or due to go on sale: MADE_AVAILABLE or PLANNED.
worked_example.no: Used only inside your own company: OWN_USE_ONLY.

facts.user_why: The CRA applies to products supplied on the EU market. If you plan to sell in the EU, we answer for the moment the product goes on sale. Showing a prototype at a fair, or using something only inside your own company, is not supplying it.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation applies to products with digital elements made available on the market
the supply of a product with digital elements for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity

facts.question: Does the product have any way to exchange data at all: network, radio, cable, USB, memory card, or a software interface?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1), 3(8)-(10). If there is no interface of any kind, no connection can be intended or foreseen (SCP-06).

worked_example.yes: A USB port used to read logs.
worked_example.no: A sealed device with no data interface of any kind.

facts.user_why: The CRA covers products that can exchange data with something else. If your product has no way at all to exchange data (no network, radio, cable, USB, card slot or software interface), it is outside the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network
including through electrical, optical or mechanical interfaces, wires or radio waves

facts.question: Is the product intended to exchange data with another device or network, directly or indirectly?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1) 'intended purpose ... includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection'. Indirect counts: a sensor talking only to a hub (SCP-05). If the answer is no, CONNECTION_FORESEEABLE is asked (SCP-07).

worked_example.yes: Sends readings to a hub, or exchanges files with a PC over USB.
worked_example.no: A connector that exists but is documented as disabled and unused: then the foreseeable-use question decides.

facts.user_why: What counts is whether exchanging data is part of how the product is meant to be used. It does not have to be the internet: a USB cable, Bluetooth, or a link through another device all count.

legal_basis.quote: the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use of which includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network
a connection to a device or network, which does not take place directly but rather as part of a larger system

facts.question: Do any of these apply to the product? Tick all that apply, or none.
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(2)-(7) and Del. Reg. 2025/1535. One question over an OR-joined list: unticked options are answered 'no'. Each ticked option opens one follow-up, because each exclusion has its own condition.

worked_example.yes: Ticks 'two- or three-wheel vehicle or quadricycle' for a connected moped.
worked_example.no: Ticks nothing: no exclusion applies.

facts.user_why: Some products are covered by other EU laws instead of the CRA. Tick only what applies; each exclusion has its own condition, which the next question checks. If none applies, tick nothing.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to products with digital elements to which the following Union legal acts apply
This Regulation does not apply to spare parts

facts.question: Is it CE-marked as a medical or in vitro diagnostic device, or does it have a medical purpose without being certified as one?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(2)(a)(b). Only a product to which MDR/IVDR applies is excluded. A medical purpose without certification is a qualification question under MDR, outside this tool (EXC-03).

worked_example.yes: CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
worked_example.no: A wellness device with no medical claim.

facts.user_why: Medical devices are excluded only if the medical device rules actually apply to them. A product with a medical purpose that is not certified as a medical device raises a question about those rules, which this tool cannot answer.

legal_basis.quote: (a) Regulation (EU) 2017/745; (b) Regulation (EU) 2017/746

facts.question: Is it a vehicle, system or component type-approved under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(2)(c). Applies to what that Regulation covers; equipment used to test vehicles is not covered (UG-06). Unclear component status goes to review (EXC-04).

worked_example.yes: An in-vehicle system covered by the vehicle's type approval.
worked_example.no: Test equipment used in vehicle development.

facts.user_why: Vehicles and their parts are excluded where the vehicle type-approval rules cover them. Equipment used to develop or test vehicles is not covered by those rules, so it stays under the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: (c) Regulation (EU) 2019/2144

facts.question: Is it certified in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(3) excludes only products certified under it; falling within its scope is not enough (EXC-07).

worked_example.yes: An avionics unit with its certification documents.
worked_example.no: Ground equipment within the regulation's scope but not certified.

facts.user_why: Aviation products are excluded only if they are actually certified under the EU aviation rules. Being the kind of product those rules cover is not enough.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to products with digital elements that have been certified in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139

facts.question: Is it marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU?

worked_example.yes: Navigation equipment for ships, wheel-marked under the Directive.
worked_example.no: A consumer boat accessory outside that Directive.

facts.user_why: Marine equipment covered by the EU marine equipment rules is excluded from the CRA.

legal_basis.quote: This Regulation does not apply to equipment that falls within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU

facts.question: Is it a two- or three-wheel vehicle or quadricycle under Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, or a system or component for one? Is it an L1e vehicle designed to pedal?
facts.why_we_ask: Del. Reg. (EU) 2025/1535 excludes products under Reg. 168/2013, except L1e vehicles designed to pedal (EXC-11, EXC-12).

worked_example.yes: A connected moped: L_CATEGORY.
worked_example.no: A speed pedelec: L1E_DESIGNED_TO_PEDAL, which stays in scope.

facts.user_why: Mopeds, motorcycles, three-wheelers and quadricycles are excluded by a separate act. Light vehicles designed to be pedalled, such as speed pedelecs, are not excluded.

legal_basis.quote: However, that exclusion shall not apply to L1e category vehicles designed to pedal

facts.question: Is it a spare part replacing an identical component, made to the same specifications?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(6). A replacement with improved or different specifications is not excluded (BND-06, BND-07).

worked_example.yes: Same board, same specifications, sold as a replacement.
worked_example.no: A replacement module with an upgraded radio.

facts.user_why: A spare part that replaces an identical component, made to the same specifications, is excluded. A replacement with different or improved specifications is a product in its own right.

legal_basis.quote: spare parts that are made available on the market to replace identical components in products with digital elements and that are manufactured according to the same specifications as the components that they are intended to replace

facts.question: Was it developed or modified exclusively for national security or defence, or specifically designed to process classified information?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(7). Dual-use products are not excluded (EXC-09). Because exclusion is the permissive answer, it needs documentary support (EXC-05, EXC-14).

worked_example.yes: A device built only under a defence contract, with the contract as evidence.
worked_example.no: A product sold to both civilian and military buyers: DUAL_USE.

facts.user_why: Products made only for national security or defence are excluded. A product also sold for civilian use is not. Because this exclusion takes a product out of the CRA, you will need documents that show it.

legal_basis.quote: developed or modified exclusively for national security or defence purposes or to products specifically designed to process classified information

facts.question: Does it collect, process and store meter data or personal data?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02: 'collect, process and store meter or personal data'.

worked_example.yes: Stores consumption readings and forwards them to the utility.
worked_example.no: Displays a reading but stores and processes nothing.

facts.revision: v2 (added when building the screens; used by the WP7 trial rules)
facts.user_why: A smart meter gateway collects, processes and stores meter data or personal data. This is one of five functions that together make a gateway.

legal_basis.quote: collect, process and store meter or personal data

facts.question: Does it protect data and information flows by supporting specific cryptographic needs, such as encrypting and decrypting data for the metering system?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02: 'protect data and information flows by supporting specific cryptographic needs, such as encryption and decryption of data'.

worked_example.yes: Encrypts and decrypts the metering system's communication with third parties.
worked_example.no: Uses TLS only for its own firmware downloads.

facts.revision: v2 (added when building the screens; used by the WP7 trial rules)
facts.question_hint: This is about protecting the metering system's data flows, not only the device's own connection.
facts.user_why: A smart meter gateway protects the metering system's data by encrypting and decrypting it. Using encryption only for the device's own connection is not this function.

legal_basis.quote: protect data and information flows by supporting specific cryptographic needs, such as encryption and decryption of data

facts.question: Does it incorporate firewalling functionality for the metering system?
facts.why_we_ask: IV-02: 'incorporate firewalling functionalities'.

worked_example.yes: Filters and restricts traffic between the home metering network and the outside.
worked_example.no: Has no traffic filtering of its own.

facts.revision: v2 (added when building the screens; used by the WP7 trial rules)
facts.user_why: A smart meter gateway filters and restricts traffic for the metering system, like a firewall.

legal_basis.quote: incorporate firewalling functionalities

facts.question: What is your product mainly for?
facts.why_we_ask: Purpose screen over the encoded categories' core-purpose facts. OR-joined list: each unticked option is a user-confirmed 'no' that rules out its categories at once; ticked options open their detailed questions. Options describe purposes, not category names. Grows with each encoded category.
facts.user_why: To say a product is not in a listed category, the tool has to rule that category out. This question rules out the ones that clearly do not fit, so you are only asked about the ones that might.

legal_basis.quote: Products with digital elements which have the core functionality of a product category set out in Annex III shall be considered to be important products

worked_example.yes: A smart door lock: ticks 'protecting a home or the people in it'.
worked_example.no: A rodent-detecting camera for pest control: ticks nothing.

facts.revision: v2 (purpose screen, added when building the screens)

facts.question: Does the product have a radio: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, a mobile network, NFC, LoRa or another wireless link?
facts.why_we_ask: Gate for Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30: it applies only to radio equipment (Directive 2014/53/EU).
facts.user_why: Products with a radio may already have cybersecurity rules under the radio equipment rules, since 1 August 2025, before the CRA applies.

legal_basis.quote: shall apply to any radio equipment that can communicate itself over the internet

facts.question: Can the product itself communicate over the internet, directly or through other equipment such as a phone, hub or router?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 1(1): internet-connected radio equipment is covered (RED Art. 3(3)(d)).
facts.user_why: Any radio product that can reach the internet, even through a phone or hub, is covered by the radio equipment cybersecurity rules.

legal_basis.quote: radio equipment that can communicate itself over the internet, whether it communicates directly or via any other equipment

facts.question: Is the product a toy, made only for childcare, or worn on the body or on clothing?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 1(2)(b)-(d): these are covered even without an internet connection, if they can process personal, traffic or location data.
facts.user_why: Toys, childcare products and wearables are covered by the radio equipment rules even without an internet connection, if they handle personal data.

legal_basis.quote: radio equipment designed or intended exclusively for childcare
to be worn on, strapped to, or hung from any of the following

facts.question: Can the product process personal data, or traffic or location data? For example names, recordings, health readings or where someone is.
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 1(2): the condition for the categories in points (b)-(d).
facts.user_why: For toys, childcare products and wearables, the radio equipment rules apply when the product can handle personal, traffic or location data.

legal_basis.quote: if that radio equipment is capable of processing

facts.question: Does the product exchange data with other devices or networks?
facts.why_we_ask: Art. 2(1) connection test as one question: intended purpose OR reasonably foreseeable use includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection. Replaces asking DATA_INTERFACE_PRESENT, CONNECTION_INTENDED and CONNECTION_FORESEEABLE one by one; those are asked only after 'Not sure'.
facts.user_why: The CRA covers products whose intended or reasonably foreseeable use includes exchanging data with a device or network. It does not have to be the internet: a cable, USB, Bluetooth, or a link through another device all count.

legal_basis.quote: the intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use of which includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network
a connection to a device or network, which does not take place directly but rather as part of a larger system

evidence_note: Tranche 1 of the collection found that decidability splits by product class rather than by fact: hardware datasheets state decisive conditions explicitly and are backed by certification registries, while software product pages state marketing claims that vendors define differently. The same fact can therefore be DOCUMENT_LIKELY for a hardware product and MANUFACTURER_ONLY for a software one. See wp2-collection-tranche-1.md.
revision_note: v2, 2026-10-12, from the WP7 trial: conditions the law joins with AND are separate facts, because a 'No' must say which condition failed; conditions joined with OR may share a question. Facts that can reach a legally open question carry condition_values mapping to OPEN. Superseded facts are kept with superseded_by for traceability.
